parsed.explanation: Combined federal-state regime imposes birth-sex passport, facility and document rules on every outed visitor, with entry refusal and possible fraud ineligibility, trespass arrest and birth-sex custody, and documented severe detention abuse if detained. No death penalty or organised sweeps, near-baseline trans homicide, and functioning courts, injunctions and national prosecution prevent lower scores. State adds worst-tier erasure, school facility ban, no state GI protections and no minor care. Remedies are real but slow and do not cancel universal exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary definition; X passports not newly issued, M/F per birth-sex documents; discrepancy cable encourages refusal and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; no automatic permanent finding; ACLU passport suit and court challenges pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from refusal to fraud allegation and detention/removal, interacting with state ID invalidation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Bathroom trespass arrest with 24 hours in men's ward; federal prison conversion/hormone removal; immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires wilful entry plus refusal to depart; pretrial release obtained; courts and counsel available.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility or document enforcement leads to arrest, then birth-sex placement and reported custodial abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal government facilities barred congruent with identity; this state requires public-school facilities by birth and is tabulated for 2024-25 bathroom/facility bans.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No generic visitor facility protection documented in this state; bans in mapped states are government-focused.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal and state birth-sex rules stack across federal buildings, schools and state facilities with no operative pre-emption for visitors.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care under 18 and closed main adolescent clinic; federal custody removes hormones; proposed federal insurance bar for minors.
care_services.protection: Not documented for adult visitor hormone continuity or emergency trans-specific care.
care_services.interaction: Custody or facility discovery can become care denial; minor visitor cannot access banned care in-state.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders define sex by birth, rescind trans protections, investigate schools, and counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; reward memo not using ideology as criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked/enjoined; national hate-crime law and employment ruling remain; marriage recognition protected.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing reinforces federal enforcement but courts sometimes restrain executive action.

minors_guardians.exposure: School bathrooms by birth, sports sex verification, under-18 care ban, supreme-court denial of teen name change despite parental consent, and federal threat to teachers facilitating transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented for visiting minors; parental consent did not secure name change.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with minor faces school facility, care and document exposures beyond adult visitor risks.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime law excludes gender identity; religious-liberties statute allows service refusals; trans-women killing rate 6.6/100k vs 6.0 general, near baseline; last documented state killing 2017.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National prosecution gave 49-year sentence for 2017 bias murder; 67% polling support anti-discrimination protections; municipal ordinances in four cities.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No state GI recourse increases street/service vulnerability, partially offset by federal prosecution.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order litigation unresolved; state has no GI employment/housing/public-accommodations protection; enforcement of adult facility bans not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, civil-liberties suit, injunctions on some orders, courts ordering release in cited cases.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may limit particular federal measures but do not restore facility, document or state protections during travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1 birth-sex placement, documented men's-ward hold and custodial harm, slow remedies. This case has stronger courts, legal aid and near-baseline violence, so slightly higher than 0.25.
Both involve routine exclusion without likely imprisonment or execution. Here entry fraud ineligibility, criminal trespass and severe detention reports exceed mere exclusion, so lower than 0.35.
0.55 involves secondary screening, delay and discretionary refusal with working appeals. This case adds criminal facility exposure, universal birth-sex rules and custody abuse, so materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is federal birth-sex documents and facilities plus a state worst-tier overlay: school facility exclusion, invalidated non-birth-sex licences, no GI anti-discrimination law, and a minor-care ban. Discovery at border, checkpoints or facilities can lead to refusal, possible permanent fraud finding, trespass arrest and birth-sex custody where abuse is documented. Courts, injunctions, existing X validity, municipal protections and a successful federal bias prosecution are operative mitigations, but they do not pre-empt the stacked exposures. No execution pathway or organised targeting is documented.
